messages:
Vikram: Quick RFC — prototype for cache handshake on driver/runtime/model changes. Need opinions on keying, persistence, and invalidation semantics. TL;DR: cohorted keys + versioned namespace + soft TTL + explicit invalidation on driver/model delta. Thoughts?

Rachael: Clarify triggers — what exactly causes an invalidate? full driver binary hash? model manifest bump? runtime flags?

Vikram: The idea is a composite trigger: driver_build_id (git sha or build id) + model_manifest.version. Also include kernel-selector fingerprint for cases where we only change kernel selection logic. We want to avoid full catastrophic wipes if compatibility can be proven.

Sam: FWIW we saw perf regressions after a small selector tweak last week — stale KV reuse led to wrong kernel path and tail latency spike. Microbench: cold-miss token cost ~1.2ms, misses under heavy seqlen skew jumped to ~5ms due to cache churn.

Jen: For persistence: write keys under namespaces with a rev id, e.g. `ns:{model_v}:{driver_rev}:{kernel_fingerprint}`. Keep soft-ttl (6h) and allow async GC of old rev namespaces. That gives fast rollback and cheap switch-over.

Marko: Can also do pointer-swap: build new namespace, warm it, then atomically flip a namespace pointer used by the router. Avoids cross-contamination.

Rachael: How do we handle small selector-only changes? Full invalidation seems heavy.

Vikram: Exactly — plan is to include `kernel_selector_hash` in keying, but also maintain compatibility metadata per kernel_fingerprint. If compatibility table says old->new compatible (no KV layout change), we can reuse keys. Otherwise, invalidate just that cohort.

Sam: Proposed key format (proto):
```
key = sha1(prefix || model_id || model_ver || driver_rev || kernel_hash || seqlen_bin || arch)
```
seqlen_bin is critical — we've been getting incorrect cache hits from mixing different sequence-length bins which breaks KV offsets.

perf-bot: Profiling sample (flamegraph slice) — shows hot path during churn:
```
0.6%  runtime::kv::get
0.4%  runtime::kernel_selector::choose
0.3%  runtime::batcher::flush
0.2%  runtime::kv::evict
```
Note: kv::evict spikes align with driver swaps.

Jen: For GC strategy: async sweep process that lists rev namespaces and GC if older than N revisions or older than TTL. For enterprise where persistence matters, provide explicit `invalidate_rev` API that marks a rev as deprecated and kicks async rewarm jobs.

Marko: One caveat — atomic pointer-swap requires consensus across router instances. We'll need a config-plane message (etcd/consul) to flip the live namespace. Race window must be tiny.

Rachael: Can we add heuristics to avoid invalidating cohorts with >X% hit-rate? If a cohort is hot and compatible, keep it even if driver_rev changes, as long as compatibility says safe.

Vikram: Good call. Compatibility checks + heat-based retention. Also add metrics: per-cohort hit-rate, avg latency, last-write-rev. Use these to drive auto-eviction policies.

Sam: Test plan: harness that toggles `kernel_selector` flag and runs 10k inferences across seqlen distribution (p95,p99) and measures tail impact. Quick example run: 
```
before: p99=42ms, after-selector-tweak (no invalidation): p99=72ms
after: p99=45ms (with cohort invalidation)
```
Shows cost of not invalidating.

Jen: Edge cases: model re-quantize (int8->int4) will definitely break KV layout. That should force global invalidation. Mark as non-compatible.

Vikram: Action items: Sam + Jen to prototype the namespace + pointer-swap flow + GC api. Rachael/Marko to sketch compatibility table schema (what signals mean compatible). I'll mock up the key-format code and a perf harness to reproduce regression. Aim for a demo by Monday. :thumbsup:

Sam: On it — will add a perf dashboard and regression job.

Jen: I’ll draft GC + invalidate_rev API.

Rachael: Will start the compatibility schema doc. :eyes:

Marko: I'll prototype pointer flip in staging and test race scenarios.

perf-bot: Noted: created perf job `cache-handshake-seqlen-proto` (ID 7642). Scheduled daily.

Vikram: Thanks all. If anyone has existing scripts that showed the selector-induced regression, drop them here. Otherwise I'll post my microbench output later today.
